sentences.text: Learned Senior counsel has straightaway drawn the attention of this court towards the judgment delivered in the case of Inderjit Walia Vs. State of M.P. passed in Misc. Cr. Case No. 8517/2014 decided on 27-11-2014, which was filed by the co-accused ie Accused No.2 .

entities.text: Inderjit Walia Vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that allegations against the present petitioner and against the co-accused Mr Inderjit Walia were almost identical in nature.

The relevant concluding paragraphs No. 10 and 11 passed in connected MCRC No. 8517/2014 reads as under:-
"10.

Thus it is settled law that when the complaint is lodged after the expiry of the shelf life of the sample , then the vendor is deprived of his right to get analyze another sample by Central Food Laboratory.
In the present case both the samples expire their shelf life on 16-01-2011 and 26-02-2011; whereas the complaint has been filed on 23-09-2011.
The complaint has been filed after lapse of seven months.
In such a situation the petitioner is deprived of his valuable right under Section 13(2) of the Act to sent the other part of the sample to Director Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
11. In the result, the petition is allowed.

Criminal Case No. 18702/2011 pending before JMFC, Indore and order dated 23-09-2011 taking cognizance against the petitioner for the offenses punishable under Sections 7/16 (1) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are hereby quashed and the petitioner is discharged from all the charges."
In light of the aforesaid, the present MCRC also stands allowed.

Criminal Case No. 18702/2011 as well as order dated 23-09-2011 passed by the JMFC, Indore taking cognizance of the offences punishable u/s 7 and 16 of the Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act, 1954 are hereby quashed and the petitioner is discharged from all the charges.
